summary: Masamichi Sakai works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Sakai studied at the University of Vienna, receiving a Dr.phil. (attested 2010), and was supervised by Helmut Krasser in 2006.
Masanori Nakagawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (attested 1991) and an associate professor in the Faculty of Letters (attested 2002) at Chikushi Jogakuen University.

Masanori Shono is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. Shono held an assistant professor post at Osaka University (attested 2012) and was a researcher at the University of Munich (attested 2015).

Masao Abe (1915–2006) specialized in philosophy and Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Kyoto University and in the US under Reinhold Niebuhr and Paul Tillich. He held professorships at Nara University, Kyoto University, Hanazono University, and the University of Hawaiʻi.

Masao Shizutani (b. 1923) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. Shizutani held associate professorships at Josai University and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (attested 1974).

Masao Yamaguchi (1931–2013) worked in religious studies and Japanology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Tokyo Metropolitan University, he taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1965–1989), the University of Shizuoka, and served as president of Sapporo University (1999).
Masaru Akimoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Akimoto served as a professor in the Faculty of Contemporary Society at Kyoto Women's University (attested 2002, 2015).

Masashi Nagai (b. 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned master's and doctoral degrees from Komazawa University. He served Komazawa University as lecturer, associate professor, professor emeritus (2017), and president (2019), and worked at the Soto Zen Research Center.
Masataka Suzuki (b. 1949) specializes in religious studies. He studied at Keio University from around 1968 to 1979 and later held a post there from around 1986 to 2015.

Masataro Sawayanagi (1865–1927) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1885–1888). He held posts at Tokyo University of Education (~1910–1911), Tohoku University (~1911–1913), Kyushu University, and Taisho University (~1926–1927).

Masato Kobayashi (b. 1970) specializes in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD ~1995–2000 under George Cardona), and held a research fellow post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (~2000–2003).

Masatoshi Konishi (1938–2020) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at ICU, the University of Calcutta, the University of Tokyo, and Rikkyo University, he taught at Hosei University (1971–1984) and Rikkyo University (1984–2003, Professor Emeritus).

Masatoshi Nagatomi (1926–2000) was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Ryukoku University, Kyoto University, and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as an instructor of Sanskrit at Harvard beginning in 1958.

Masayuki Taira (b. 1951) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1970–1980) and held posts at Kansai University (~1985–1994), Osaka University (~1994–2017), and Kyoto Tachibana University (~2017).

Massimo Pallottino (1909–1995) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Rome (~1927–1931) and held academic posts at the University of Cagliari (~1940–1945) and the University of Rome (~1946–1980).
Masumi Mochizuki (b. 1958) is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Minobusan University as a lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies (attested 2001) and as a professor (attested 2015).

Mathieu Boisvert is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under Anthony Kennedy Warder and Ravindra Panth. He became a professor at Université du Québec à Montréal in 1992 and founded the Groupe de recherches interdisciplinaire sur le Montréal ethno-religieux.

Matteo Bartoli (1873–1946) was a linguist. He studied at the University of Vienna (~1894–1898) and under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1898–1900), and held a post at the University of Turin from around 1907 to 1946.

Matthew B. Orsborn specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong by 2012 under supervisors Guang Xing and Y. Karunadasa, and studied under traditional teachers Hsing Yun and Huishang.
Matthew Clark works in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Daud Ali and George Botterill, earning his PhD from SOAS University of London between 1999 and 2004.
